title: How to Unlock Your Real Personality
coreMove: Treat social feedback as a steering signal, not a stop sign; let speech, volume, warmth, and action move before self-criticism hardens into inhibition.

exampleSpecs.audience: Murray, a volunteer speaker rehearsing a short toast
exampleSpecs.stakes: A careful rehearsal can turn negative feedback and self-criticism into more stuttering.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Show overmonitoring of speech creating the very block it tries to prevent.

exampleSpecs.audience: Diego, a team lead presenting a prototype
exampleSpecs.stakes: Smiles, frowns, and body language can inform rapport without taking over the exchange.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Treat social signals as information instead of a verdict.

exampleSpecs.audience: Farah, a trainer leading a staff drill
exampleSpecs.stakes: A louder voice can act as a disinhibitor when quiet expression has become the default.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use volume as a bodily route into freer expression.

exampleSpecs.audience: Gaelle, a cafe owner practicing direct warmth
exampleSpecs.stakes: Compliments and expressed liking can turn private approval into free expression.

exampleSpecs.audience: Bohdan, a supervisor repairing a delivery route
exampleSpecs.stakes: Waiting for perfect certainty can prevent the feedback that correction needs.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Begin action before the plan feels complete.

exampleSpecs.audience: Tracy, a receptionist reviewing patient calls
exampleSpecs.stakes: Constant self-criticism can masquerade as useful correction.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Separate one practical repair from a pile of self-attacks.
